ROBOTECH is a student-led HealthTech initiative focused on improving maternal-care access and safety in underserved communities through a strict, phased approach. Our core belief is simple: pregnancy care is high-stakes, so we build with discipline safety-first, research-first, and non-clinical-first. We start by solving problems that are safe to build today (coordination, workflow, and access), while preparing long-term research foundations for robotics-enabled assistance in the future.

Our current focus is “Health Connect” a privacy-first, non-clinical booking and care-coordination system designed to reduce delays and missed access. Health Connect supports appointment requests, OTP verification, admin approvals, slot assignment, reschedule/cancel flows, and status tracking with minimal data capture. We do not collect sensitive identity documents (e.g., Aadhaar) or medical history in V0, and we avoid clinical claims. The goal is to create a working prototype and real operational learning that can scale responsibly.

ROBOTECH is built by an interdisciplinary team across Biomedical Research, Product (UI/UX + Frontend/Backend + App), Electronics & Embedded Systems, Cybersecurity/Cloud, and Mechanical Research. We operate like an execution-driven early-stage startup: clear roles, weekly deliverables, documentation discipline, and proof over presentations. Our roadmap is phased establish constraints and boundaries, build a functioning MVP, validate workflows through pilots, then expand engineering depth and research capability step-by-step.

We collaborate with students, early professionals, researchers, and institutions who value real-world impact, consistency, and long-term thinking. If you align with disciplined building and meaningful healthcare innovation, connect with us to collaborate.

The Centre of Excellence on Biologically Inspired Robots and Drones (BIRD) at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) is a multidisciplinary initiative focused on advancing robotics and aerial systems inspired by nature.

BIRD aims to explore and engineer intelligent, adaptive, and efficient robotic platforms by drawing inspiration from biological systems — from insects and birds to human motion. Our research spans areas such as soft robotics, swarm intelligence, bio-mimetic drones, flapping-wing flight, autonomous navigation, and environmental interaction.

We bring together researchers, students, industry partners, and policy thinkers to develop cutting-edge technologies with real-world impact — ranging from defense and agriculture to healthcare and disaster response.

 Robotics & Advanced Control Systems

 Requirements & Validation Consulting

Our belief is simple: great engineering starts before the first line of code or circuit design. It starts with clarity — on objectives, on constraints, on what the system actually needs to do.

Description:

Name: QUANTIS AI LABS
Description:
Quantis AI Labs is building the intelligence infrastructure for autonomous systems — beginning where conditions are least forgiving: at sea.

Unmanned platforms are being procured at scale. Budgets are committed. Hulls are being launched. The constraint is no longer the vessel — it is the intelligence that makes the vessel operationally viable. Autonomy today is fragmented across point solutions, brittle outside controlled conditions, incapable of coordinating at fleet scale, and blind to its own operational data. Quantis AI Labs exists to close that gap.

We do not build vessels. We build the intelligence layer that makes vessels operationally autonomous.

The stack:

Mission Compute — proprietary deterministic mission compute: low-SWaP, modular and stackable from nano-UAV to large USV and AUV.

Perception & Navigation — sensor fusion and navigation intelligence engineered for degraded sensors, dynamic weather, and high-traffic waterways.

Mission Autonomy — mission-level decision software built for meaningful independence from human supervision. Autonomous, not remote-controlled.

Fleet Intelligence — a cloud-based coordination layer for distributed multi-vessel operations, with every mission feeding a continuous learning loop.

The same stack extends beyond the maritime domain — to robotics, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure. The sea is where it is validated first.

One platform family. Every class of unmanned system. Built to learn.

We believe robotics should amplify human capability, not replace it. Our vision is simple and demanding: one trained operator, one robot, one acre per day delivering consistent output that matches or exceeds multiple manual harvesters, without damaging plants or exhausting people.

Krisi Vahana is built by two people who refuse to stay in their lanes. Gopal, a mechanical engineer, obsesses over building machines that survive real farm conditions. Kurukshetra 2026 is a national-level technical festival designed to bring together innovation, engineering excellence, and practical problem-solving on a single high-impact platform. Name: TARVAN
Description:
TARVAN builds the Physical AI intelligence layer that upgrades industrial machines from mechanical to intelligent.

We encode the complete Sense → Think → Act loop: industrial-grade machine vision captures every object and defect at line speed. Domain-specific ML models run inference on edge compute in under 85 milliseconds. Deterministic actuators execute grading, ejection, or path corrections — timed to the millisecond, logged for full traceability.

Our technology is designed as a plug-and-play intelligence module for OEM machine builders. We don't replace your machine — we make it see, decide, and act at production speed. Zero cloud dependency. 100% edge inference.

Where we operate:
→ Inspection & Grading: Real-time quality classification with pneumatic ejection (flagship: cashew kernel grading across 4 parallel lanes at 10 kernels/sec/lane)
→ Food & Agri Sorting: Export-grade quality assurance for spices, pulses, seeds, and packaged food
→ Process Automation: Continuous path planning and servo control for industrial workflows
→ Pharma & High-Value Inspection: Precision visual inspection for compliance-critical products

Founded by Dr. Shanmugakumar Murugesan (Ph.D. CSE, IIITDM Kancheepuram; M.Des. Electronic Systems), TARVAN is incubated at IIT Kanpur SIIC and NSRCEL IIM Bangalore, and supported by grants from DST NIDHI PRAYAS, DSIR-PRISM, and RKVY Raftaar.

Description:
Cities run on invisible labour. The floors get cleaned. The corridors get sanitised. The public spaces stay usable. Behind all of it are service workers doing repetitive, physically demanding, chronically understaffed jobs that no one is solving at scale.
Pura Robotics is building the physical intelligence layer for the service robots cities need.

Not robots that follow routes. Robots that understand their environment, reason about what needs doing, and take instructions in natural language from anyone, on day one, with zero training. Robots that adapt when the world changes, not just when someone reprograms them.

We are starting with commercial indoor floor cleaning - the highest-volume, highest-labour, most structurally underserved service task in the built environment. Floor cleaning is the wedge. The ambition is every service robot a city depends on.

Physical intelligence is what makes the difference between a robot that executes and a robot that works.

Name: Team Equinox
Description:
We are proud to be part of aBAJA SAEINDIA, a national-level autonomous vehicle competition that challenges engineering students to design, build, and test an off-road buggy capable of Level 2 autonomy and beyond.

We aim to develop an autonomous all-terrain vehicle capable of intelligent decision-making, obstacle avoidance, and safe navigation in unstructured environments.

Core Capabilities of Our aBAJA Vehicle:
• Lane Keeping Assist (LKA)
• Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC)
• Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB)
• Obstacle Detection 
• Real-time Path Planning and Navigation

System Architecture Highlights:
• Onboard Processor: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano for AI & perception
• Control System: ROS 2 (Humble) powered modular software architecture
• Sensors: RADAR, GNSS/IMU, wheel encoders, and camera modules
• Drive-by-Wire: Custom EPS-based steering with absolute encoder feedback, longitudinal control through custom brake and throttle by wire mechanism for braking and acceleration
• Simulation & Testing: Validated in IPG CarMaker and RViz environments

Our development emphasizes real-time ROS 2 integration, sensor fusion, robust control systems (Stanley, PID), and a hardware-software co-design approach to bring a safe and reliable autonomous vehicle to the off-road terrain.

Our Goals:
Push the limits of autonomous mobility in challenging environments

Demonstrate reliable perception and control systems under dynamic conditions
Inspire innovation in student-driven robotics and autonomous systems

Stay tuned for more updates as we gear up for the aBAJA 2025 event at NATRAX, Pune!

Description:

For years, inventory visibility in warehouses and distribution centers has depended on manual counting, scanning, and verification, a slow, error-prone process that absorbs labor hours and never fully closes the accuracy gap. Vimaan changes that.

We call our category Inventory Intelligence: going beyond basic visibility and tracking to give operations teams the ability to capture, reconcile, and act on inventory data without a manual recount to verify it.

Our platform is built on computer vision, not legacy machine vision or barcode-dependent systems, giving teams a live, reconstructed view of physical inventory rather than just recorded transactions. Our core products, StorTRACK, PalletSCAN, and ParcelSCAN, automate cycle counting, inbound receiving, and outbound shipping on this same foundation, helping teams achieve up to 80% lower labor costs and move toward 100% inventory accuracy.

Name: Integra Robotics
Description:
A new category of general-purpose machines designed to reshape how work gets done.

Our robots adapt to any environment ranging from industrial automation to mission-critical operations through software and modular design rather than costly redesigns.

Every robot in our fleet runs on the same foundation model and core architecture. Like siblings sharing genetic code, they may perform different jobs but draw from one unified intelligence, ensuring consistency and seamless updates across the entire fleet.

When one robot learns a new skill, every robot inherits it. A fleet of 1,000 robots learning for one year delivers 1,000 years of collective experience, shared instantly with all.

Unlike traditional machinery that depreciates over time, our robots appreciate. Every deployment makes the entire fleet smarter, faster, and more capable. This is the network effect applied to physical AI, one brain powering many bodies, all learning together.

We are not just building robots. We are building a living, evolving intelligence that grows with every task, every environment, and every deployment.

Name: Social Hardware
Description:
Integra Robotics began with a simple conviction: robotics should be built by those who understand the ground reality, not imported at premium cost. What started with a patented flexible bionic hand and 150 assistive devices shipped through non-profits has evolved into India's most vertically integrated robotics platform, serving Defence, Industry, and Embodied AI.

We follow an "Origami Approach" to robotics, folding modular hardware, unified software, and shared components into a single platform. From security-based ground vehicles for suppliers to security agencies to Cobots on MSME shop floors, and robotic arms operating from factory lines to ocean depths of 300 metres, one DNA powers every deployment. With 95% in-house design, 5 patents, and NVIDIA Inception backing, every SKU we ship feeds our reinforcement learning models, compounding intelligence with every mission.

We are not competing with global incumbents on their terms. We are rewriting the economics of robotics from India, for the world.

All systems are developed in alignment with international standards, including ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 13850, and ISO 10218‐1, ensuring quality, information security, and operational safety at a global benchmark.

Name: Team Abhiyaan
Description:
Team Abhiyaan is an enthusiastic group of multi-disciplinary students of IIT Madras, committed to building intelligent, robust, precise and safe ground navigation systems. As a competition team of 45 members, we participate in an international robotics competition called IGVC (Intelligent Ground Vehicle Competition) held at Oakland University, Michigan, USA. Participants are given a problem statement using which robots have to navigate autonomously through laned obstacles in Auto Nav challenge of IGVC.
With the vision of creating autonomous navigation systems to negate human risk, we aim to designing a six-seater golf cart to operate autonomously in closed and restricted environments like institutes, airports and gated communities.
Currently Abhiyaan is also working on a project called MACRo (Martian Autonomous Core Sampling Rover) in collaboration with Extra-Terrestrial Manufacturing (ExTeM), which aims to build an autonomous rover capable of collecting core samples from Martian surfaces. The rover will be built to withstand the intense Martian conditions and we intend to drill 1 foot for more in-depth research and analysis, whereas current rovers can only drill 2.75 inches.
Our goal is to strive for and progress toward the vision of developing autonomous systems that can help solve many real-world problems and assist humans in their daily activities.
